K-345.stuck: Read the sentence again and ask the child, "Can you do that?" For the last line, a child may draw the thing and write the first letter or one word with your help.

K:alphabet-order.say: "This is a dot-to-dot with letters. Start at the letter a and draw a line to b, then to c, and keep going in ABC order until the picture is finished."
K:alphabet-order.first: Say or sing the alphabet together once, slowly. Find the dot with the letter a together and put a finger on it. Ask, "What comes after a?" Find b and draw the first line together. Tell the children to say the alphabet quietly as they go.
K:alphabet-order.stuck: Point to the row of letters at the bottom of the page: it shows the order. Have the child find the letter they are on in that row; the next letter in the row is the dot to look for. The letters on this page stop at t.

K:order-by-size.say: "Each box has three pictures: a small one, a medium one, and a big one. Write 1 on the smallest, 2 on the medium one, and 3 on the biggest."
K:order-by-size.first: Write 1, 2, 3 on the board. Do the first box together. Ask, "Which one is the smallest?" It gets the 1. "Which one is the biggest?" It gets the 3. "Which one is left?" It gets the 2.
K:order-by-size.stuck: Have the child point to the smallest and the biggest first; the one that is left is the medium one. A child who cannot write the numbers yet may copy them from the board.

K-034.say: "Each row has five pictures of the same thing in different sizes. Write 1 under the smallest, then 2, 3, 4, and 5 under the biggest."
K-034.first: Write 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 on the board. Do the first row together. Ask, "Which one is the smallest?" It gets the 1. "Which one is next?" It gets the 2. Go on until the biggest gets the 5.
K-034.stuck: Have the child find the smallest one left each time and cross it off lightly after writing its number.

K-036.say: "Each row has four pictures of the same thing. Write 1 under the shortest, then 2 and 3, and 4 under the tallest."
K-036.first: Write 1, 2, 3, 4 on the board. Do the first row together. Ask, "Which one is the shortest?" It gets the 1. "Which one is next?" It gets the 2. Go on until the tallest gets the 4.
K-036.stuck: Have the child find the shortest one left each time and cross it off lightly after writing its number.

K:position-words.say: "Look at where each animal is: on the box, under the box, or beside the box. In every picture, circle the animal that is ON the box."
K:position-words.first: Put a book on a chair, then under it, then beside it, and have the class say the word each time. Then do the first picture on the page together: "Which animal is ON the box?" Circle it. Ask about the others, too: "Which one is under the box? Which one is beside it?"
K:position-words.stuck: Have the child show the word with a hand and the desk: "Put your hand ON the desk. Now UNDER the desk." Then go back to the picture and ask the child to point to the top of the box.

K-065.say: "There is a line down the middle of the page. Circle every picture on the LEFT side of the line."
K-065.first: Have the children hold up their left hand: the thumb and pointer finger make an L. Point to the left side of the page. Find one picture on the left together and circle it.
K-065.stuck: Have the child hold up the L hand and lay it next to the page on the left side. Everything on that side of the line gets a circle.

K-066.say: "The page has three rows: the top, the middle, and the bottom. Circle every picture in the MIDDLE row."
K-066.first: Point to the top row, the middle row, and the bottom row and have the class say each word. Find one picture in the middle row together and circle it.
K-066.stuck: Have the child put one finger on the top row and one on the bottom row: the middle is between the fingers.

K-067.say: "There is a big shape on the page. Circle every picture that is INSIDE the big shape."
K-067.first: Trace the edge of the big shape with your finger. Ask, "Which pictures are inside the line? Which are outside?" Find one inside together and circle it.
K-067.stuck: Have the child trace the edge of the shape with a finger: a picture inside the line gets a circle.

position-words-shapes-k064.say: "Each card names a place: ON the box, UNDER the box, or BESIDE the box. Circle the shape that is in that place."
position-words-shapes-k064.first: Put a book on a chair, then under it, then beside it, and have the class say the word each time. Read the words under each card aloud: ON the box, UNDER the box, BESIDE the box, UNDER the box. Do the first card together: "Which shape is ON the box?" Circle it.

K:mazes.say: "Time for a maze. Start at the picture at the top and find the way to the bottom. Use your finger first, then your pencil."
K:mazes.first: Hold up the page and show the start and the goal. Trace the beginning of the way with your finger and stop at the first place where the path splits: "Which way? Let's try one." Tell the children to find the whole way with a finger before they draw.
K:mazes.stuck: Tell the child that a dead end is part of every maze: go back to the last place where the path split and try the other way. Starting from the goal and working backward also helps.

K-405.say: "Time for a maze. Find the way along the light path from the animal to its goal. Use your finger first, then your pencil."
K-405.first: Hold up the page and show where the path starts, at the animal with the arrow, and where it ends. Trace the beginning of the way with your finger and stop at the first place where the path splits: "Which way? Let's try one." Tell the children to find the whole way with a finger before they draw.

K-406.say: "Time for a maze. Help the animal get to its goal. Draw a line along the wide road and stay between its edges."
K-406.first: Hold up the page, read its title aloud, and show where the road starts, at the animal with the arrow, and where it ends. Trace the road with your finger and stop at each place where it splits: "Which way leads to the goal?" Tell the children to find the whole way with a finger before they draw.

K-407.say: "Time for a maze. Draw a line along the blue water from the start to the goal, and stay inside the water."
K-407.first: Hold up the page, read its title aloud, and show where the water starts, at the arrow, and where it ends. Trace the water with your finger and stop at each place where it splits: "Which way leads to the goal?" Tell the children to find the whole way with a finger before they draw.

K-411.say: "Read the title with me: it tells you who is going where. At every fork, take the road to the next number when you count: 1, 2, 3, all the way to 20."
K-411.first: Count from 1 to 20 aloud together. Put your finger on the start and find 1. Ask, "What comes next? Which road goes to 2?" Draw the first part together. Tell the children to say each number as they reach it.

K:spot-the-difference.say: "These two pictures look the same, but a few things have changed. Find what is different in the picture on the right and circle it."
K:spot-the-difference.first: Find one difference together: ask a child to point to it and say what changed. Circle it in the picture on the right. Tell the children to keep looking until they cannot find any more.
K:spot-the-difference.stuck: Have the child pick one thing in the left picture, find the same thing in the right picture, and ask, "Is it the same?" Then go on to the next thing, from the top of the picture to the bottom.

K-399.say: "The two pictures are the same, but three things are missing from the bottom picture. Find each empty place, circle it, and check a box for each one."
K-399.first: Hold up the page and compare the two pictures with the class, from the top down. Find one thing that is missing together and circle the empty place in the bottom picture. Check the first box.
K-399.stuck: Have the child pick one thing in the top picture and look for it in the bottom picture: "Is it there?" There are three missing things; the three boxes help them count.

K-400.say: "Each row shows the same picture two times, but one place in the right picture is different. Circle it, and check the box of that row."
K-400.first: Do the first row together: compare the left and the right picture, part by part, and find the one difference. Circle it in the right picture and check the box of the row.
K-400.stuck: Have the child cover half of each picture with a hand and compare one half at a time.

K:numeral-formation.say: "Now we practice writing numbers. Trace each number. Then write it yourself in the empty space."
K:numeral-formation.first: Write the first number of the page big on the board and say where it starts and which way it goes. Have the children write it in the air with you. They trace the number on the page and then write their own.
K:numeral-formation.stuck: Show the child where the number starts and guide the first stroke with your finger on the page. A number written backward is common at this age; show the right way once and move on.

K-237.say: "Now we practice writing numbers. Start at the orange dot and follow the arrows. Trace each number in the row."

K-467.say: "Count the pictures in each row. The number that tells how many is at the end of the row. Trace it."
K-467.first: Count the pictures of the first row aloud together, touching each one. Say the number and point to it at the end of the row. Write it big on the board and show where it starts. Then the children trace it.
K-467.stuck: Have the child touch each picture while counting. For the tracing, put your finger on the orange dot: "Start here."

K:beginning-sounds.say: "Say the name of each picture and listen for the very first sound. Then write the letter for that sound."
K:beginning-sounds.first: Name all the pictures on the page together, so that everyone uses the same word for each. On the page for everyone they are bus, hat, sun, pig, apple, dog, ball, and fish. Do the first one: say the word slowly and ask, "What is the first sound?" and then, "Which letter makes that sound?" Write the letter on the board; the children write it on the page.
K:beginning-sounds.stuck: Say the word and stretch the first sound: "mmm-oon." Have the child say it back. If the child knows the sound and not the letter, point to the letter on the classroom alphabet or write it for the child to copy.

K-228.say: "At the bottom are three boxes, each with a letter. Say the name of each picture and listen for its first sound. Draw a line from the picture to the letter it begins with."
K-228.first: Read the three letters on the boxes aloud and say their sounds. Name every picture together, so that everyone uses the same word (they are below). Do the first one together: say the word slowly and ask, "What is the first sound? Which box has that letter?" Draw the line.
K-228.stuck: Say the word and stretch the first sound. Then say the sound of each letter on the boxes and ask which one matches.

K-328.say: "Say the name of each picture. Does it begin with mmm or nnn? Circle m or n."
K-328.first: Say the sounds mmm and nnn together; feel the lips close for m. Name the pictures together: nest, necklace, moon, nose, medal, milk, nurse, mitten. Do the first one together: "nest. Does it start with mmm or nnn?" Circle n. For your own reference: n: nest, necklace, nose, nurse; m: moon, medal, milk, mitten.
K-328.stuck: Have the child say the word with a hand on the lips: for m the lips close, for n they stay open.

beginning-sounds-k228.first: Read the letters on the boxes aloud, B, C, and S, and say their sounds. Name the pictures together: star, cow, bus, cat, sun, banana, sock, ball, carrot. Do the first one together: "star. What is the first sound?" Draw a line to S. For your own reference: B: bus, banana, ball; C: cow, cat, carrot; S: star, sun, sock.

beginning-sounds-k228-2.first: Read the letters on the boxes aloud, B, C, and S, and say their sounds. Name the pictures together: cow, can (a soup can), sink, seal, salt (the salt shaker), bat, cat, bun, bus. Do the first one together: "cow. What is the first sound?" Draw a line to C. For your own reference: B: bat, bun, bus; C: cow, can, cat; S: sink, seal, salt.

beginning-sounds-k228-3.first: Read the letters on the boxes aloud, B, C, and S, and say their sounds. Name the pictures together: bed, sock, bat, car, cup, sun, cake, bus, spoon. Do the first one together: "bed. What is the first sound?" Draw a line to B. For your own reference: B: bed, bat, bus; C: car, cup, cake; S: sock, sun, spoon.

beginning-sounds-k228-4.first: Read the letters on the boxes aloud, B, C, and S, and say their sounds. Name the pictures together: seal, bag, sock, bee, cup, cake, car, bus, sink. Do the first one together: "seal. What is the first sound?" Draw a line to S. For your own reference: B: bag, bee, bus; C: cup, cake, car; S: seal, sock, sink.

beginning-sounds-k228-5.first: Read the letters on the boxes aloud, B, C, and S, and say their sounds. Name the pictures together: cake, cow, sink, bat, bee, bed, cat, sock, salt (the salt shaker). Do the first one together: "cake. What is the first sound?" Draw a line to C. For your own reference: B: bat, bee, bed; C: cake, cow, cat; S: sink, sock, salt.

K:rhyme.say: "Rhyming words sound the same at the end, like cat and hat. Draw a line from each picture on the left to the picture on the right that rhymes with it."
K:rhyme.first: Name all the pictures together, so that everyone uses the same words. Say the first picture on the left, then say it with each picture on the right: "boat, frog… boat, goat." Ask which pair sounds the same at the end. Draw that line together. For your own reference, the pairs on the page for everyone are boat and goat, bed and sled, dog and frog, cat and hat, bee and tree.
K:rhyme.stuck: Say the two words one after the other and stretch the ending: "c-AT, h-AT." If the endings sound the same, they rhyme. If the child does not know what a picture is called, tell them.

K-352.say: "In each box there are two pictures. Say both names out loud. If the two words rhyme, circle the check mark. If they do not rhyme, circle the X."
K-352.first: Say "cat, hat" and "cat, dog" and ask which pair rhymes. Name all the pictures on the page together, so that everyone uses the same words (they are below). Do the first box together: say the two words and ask, "Do they sound the same at the end?" Circle the check mark or the X.
K-352.stuck: Say the two words one after the other and stretch their endings. If the endings sound the same, they rhyme.

phonological-awareness-k232-3.first: Name all the pictures together, so that everyone uses the same words: on the left bed, bag, cat, dog, boat; on the right frog, goat, sled, hat, flag. Say the first picture on the left with each picture on the right: "bed, frog… bed, sled." Ask which pair sounds the same at the end. Draw that line together. For your own reference, the pairs are bed and sled, bag and flag, cat and hat, dog and frog, boat and goat.

phonological-awareness-k232-5.first: Name all the pictures together, so that everyone uses the same words: on the left sun, cat, boat, star, bed; on the right car, goat, bun (the bread), sled, hat. Say the first picture on the left with each picture on the right: "sun, car… sun, bun." Ask which pair sounds the same at the end. Draw that line together. For your own reference, the pairs are sun and bun, cat and hat, boat and goat, star and car, bed and sled.

rhyming-words-k352.first: Say "cat, hat" and "cat, dog" and ask which pair rhymes. Name the pictures together, two by two: cake and hand, boat and shirt, lock and sock, bag and duck, car and guitar, rug and brain, log and frog, hat and cat (the last animal is a cat). Do the first box together and circle the check mark or the X. For your own reference, these rhyme: lock and sock, car and guitar, log and frog, hat and cat; the other four do not.

rhyming-words-k352-2-at.first: Say "cat, hat" and "cat, dog" and ask which pair rhymes. Name the pictures together, two by two: hand and sand, balloon and raccoon, sheep and jeep, pan and chair, car and crane, hat and bat, letter (the envelope) and bread, shirt and map. Do the first box together and circle the check mark or the X. For your own reference, these rhyme: hand and sand, balloon and raccoon, sheep and jeep, hat and bat; the other four do not.

rhyming-words-k352-3-at.first: Say "cat, hat" and "cat, dog" and ask which pair rhymes. Name the pictures together, two by two: bat and cat, moose and deer, cap and map, snail and nail, train and balloon, nest and swing, bed and rake, pear and chair. Do the first box together and circle the check mark or the X. For your own reference, these rhyme: bat and cat, cap and map, snail and nail, pear and chair; the other four do not.

rhyming-words-k352-4-at.first: Say "cat, hat" and "cat, dog" and ask which pair rhymes. Name the pictures together, two by two: nest and vest, can and coat, lock and elf, glass and truck, jeep and sheep, bat and hat, map and cap, log and sled. Do the first box together and circle the check mark or the X. For your own reference, these rhyme: nest and vest, jeep and sheep, bat and hat, map and cap; the other four do not.

K:count-how-many.say: "Count the shapes in each box. Touch each one as you count. Then write the number."
K:count-how-many.first: Count the first box aloud together, touching each shape on your page as the class counts. Ask, "So how many are there?" Write the number on the board. Then write the numbers 1 to 10 on the board and leave them there for children who need to copy them.
K:count-how-many.stuck: Have the child cross out each shape while counting it, so that none is counted twice. If the child does not know how to write the number, point to it on the board.

K-002.say: "Count the pictures in each box. Touch each one as you count. Then circle the number that tells how many."
K-002.first: Count the first box aloud together, touching each picture on your page as the class counts. Ask, "So how many are there?" Circle that number among the numbers in the box.

K-027.say: "The pictures in each box stand in rows. Count all of them. Then write how many there are in all."
K-027.first: Count the first box aloud together, one row at a time, touching each picture as the class counts. Ask, "So how many are there in all?" Write the number on the board. Then write the numbers 1 to 20 on the board and leave them there for children who need to copy them.

K-640.say: "Count all the pictures in each box. There are between 11 and 20. Write how many there are in all."
K-640.first: Count the first box aloud together, touching each picture as the class counts. Ask, "So how many are there?" Write the number on the board. Then write the numbers 1 to 20 on the board and leave them there for children who need to copy them.

K:count-forward-missing.say: "Some numbers on these number strips are missing. Count along the strip and write each number that is missing."
K:count-forward-missing.first: Write the numbers 1 to 10 on the board. Count the first strip aloud together, pointing to each box, and clap at the empty box: "one, two, (clap), four." Ask, "What number goes here?" Write it in. The children do the other strips the same way.
K:count-forward-missing.stuck: Have the child read the first number of the strip and count on aloud from it, touching each box; the number they say at the empty box is the one to write. A child who does not know how to write a number may copy it from the board.

K-020.first: Write the numbers 1 to 20 on the board; the strips on this page go up to 20, and they do not all start at 1. Read the first strip aloud together, pointing to each box, and clap at each empty box: "five, (clap), seven, eight." Ask, "What number goes here?" Write it in. The children do the other strips the same way.

K-632.first: Write the numbers 1 to 100 in rows of ten on the board, or point to the class hundred chart. The strips on this page start at big numbers. Read the first strip aloud together, pointing to each box, and clap at each empty box. Ask, "What number goes here?" Write it in. The children do the other strips the same way.

K:colour-by-number.say: "Each shape on this page has a number in it. The code at the top tells you which color goes with each number. Color every shape in the color of its number."
K:colour-by-number.first: Make sure every child has the crayons the code names. Read the code aloud together. Take the first number of the code, find one shape with that number in it, and color it together. Tell the children to do one color at a time.
K:colour-by-number.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the number inside the shape, then find the same number in the code. If a child does not have a color, another color is fine as long as they use the same one for that number every time.

K:dot-to-dot-sequence.say: "This is a dot-to-dot. Start at the orange dot, at number 1. Draw a line to 2, then to 3, and keep counting until you get to 10."
K:dot-to-dot-sequence.first: Count from 1 to 10 aloud together. Find the orange dot together and put a finger on it. Ask, "What comes after 1?" Find 2 and draw the first line together.
K:dot-to-dot-sequence.stuck: Have the child say the number they are on and count one more; that is the number to look for. Point to the part of the page where the next dot is. If a line went to the wrong dot, leave it and go on from the right one.

K-285.say: "This is a dot-to-dot. Start at the orange dot, at number 1. Draw a line to 2, then to 3, and keep counting until you get to 20."
K-285.first: Count from 1 to 20 aloud together. Find the orange dot together and put a finger on it. Ask, "What comes after 1?" Find 2 and draw the first line together. The numbers 1 to 20 are printed at the bottom of the page to help.

K-295.say: "This is a dot-to-dot. Start at the orange dot, at number 11. Draw a line to 12, then to 13, and keep counting until you get to 20."
K-295.first: Count from 11 to 20 aloud together. Find the orange dot, number 11, together and put a finger on it. Ask, "What comes after 11?" Find 12 and draw the first line together.

K-296.say: "This is a dot-to-dot. Start at the orange dot, at number 11. Count on and draw a line to each next number, all the way to 30."
K-296.first: Count from 11 to 30 aloud together. Find the orange dot, number 11, together and put a finger on it. Find 12 and draw the first line together. The numbers 11 to 30 are printed at the bottom of the page to help.

K:sound-position.say: "Say the name of each picture and listen for the LAST sound, the sound at the very end. Then write the letter for that sound."
K:sound-position.first: Name all the pictures together. On the page for everyone they are fox, sun, bus, book, bed, drum, pig, and cat. Do one together: say the word slowly and hold the last sound: "bus-sss." Ask, "What is the last sound? Which letter makes that sound?" Write the letter on the board. Remind the children that this page asks for the end of the word, not the beginning.
K:sound-position.stuck: Say the word, stop before the last sound, and let the child finish it: "bu…" "sss!" A child who writes the first letter has listened to the beginning; say the word once more and tap the table at the last sound.

K-227.say: "Say the name of each picture and listen for the sound in the MIDDLE. Write the vowel you hear: a, e, i, o, or u."
K-227.first: Write a, e, i, o, u on the board. Name the pictures together: bed, dog, fox, hen, cat, bus, fig, mug. Do the first one together: say "b-e-d" slowly and stretch the middle: "beeed." Ask, "Which vowel?" Write e. For your own reference: bed e, dog o, fox o, hen e, cat a, bus u, fig i, mug u.
K-227.stuck: Say the word slowly and hold the middle sound. Then say each vowel sound on the board and ask which one matches.

K:count-syllables.say: "Words have beats, like music. The beats are called syllables. Say the name of each picture, clap the beats, and write how many claps you made."
K:count-syllables.first: Clap a few children's names together: "Ma-ri-a, three claps." Name all the pictures on the page together. On the page for everyone they are airplane (2), ambulance (3), banana (3), dog (1), sun (1), cat (1), apron (2), and acorn (2). Clap the first picture's word together and write the number on the board.
K:count-syllables.stuck: Have the child put a hand under the chin and say the word at normal speed: the chin drops once for each syllable. If the child claps every sound, say the word together the way you would say it when talking.

K-234.say: "Words have beats, called syllables. Say the name of each picture and clap its beats. Draw a line to the box with that number: 1, 2, or 3."
K-234.first: Clap a few children's names together. Name the pictures together: acorn, sun, apron, airplane, dog, ambulance, cat, banana, astronaut. Clap the first word together and draw its line. For your own reference: 1 beat: sun, dog, cat; 2 beats: acorn, apron, airplane; 3 beats: ambulance, banana, astronaut.

phonological-awareness-k233-2.first: Clap a few children's names together: "Ma-ri-a, three claps." Name all the pictures together: domino, eraser, oval, ant, tomato, bat, baby, bed. The second picture is an eraser, not lipstick. Clap the first picture's word together and write the number on the board. For your own reference: domino 3, eraser 3, oval 2, ant 1, tomato 3, bat 1, baby 2, bed 1.

K:word-sentence-tracing.say: "These are words we see all the time. Read the word, trace it, and then write it yourself on the empty line."
K:word-sentence-tracing.first: Read the words on the page aloud and have the class read each one after you. Do the first word together: read it, write it on the board, trace over it with your finger, and write it once more next to it. Tell the children to say the word each time they finish writing it.
K:word-sentence-tracing.stuck: Read the word for the child and have the child say it back while pointing to it. For the writing, have the child copy one letter at a time and keep the letters close together.

K-284.say: "Say the name of each picture. Its word is written next to it. Trace the dashed letters, then write the word yourself on the empty lines."
K-284.first: Name the pictures together and read each word aloud. Do the first word together: read it, trace over it with your finger, and write it once more on the board, saying each letter.

K-289.say: "Each picture has its word next to it. Read the word, trace the dashed word, then write it on the empty line."
K-289.first: Name the pictures together and read each word aloud. Do the first word together: read it, trace it with your finger, and write it on the board once more, saying each letter.

K-291.say: "These words are long. Read each word with me, trace it, and then write it yourself on the empty line."
K-291.first: Name the pictures together and read each long word aloud, clapping its parts: "skate-board." Do the first word together: trace it with your finger and write it on the board, one part at a time.

K:compare-groups.say: "In each box there are two groups. Count both groups. Then circle the group that has MORE."
K:compare-groups.first: Do the first box together: count one group aloud, then the other. Ask, "Which number is more?" Circle that group. Tell the children that a group can look big and still have fewer things in it, so they have to count.
K:compare-groups.stuck: Have the child draw a line from each thing in one group to one thing in the other group. The group with things left over has more.

K-009.say: "In each box there are two groups. Count both groups. Then circle the group that has FEWER."
K-009.first: Do the first box together: count one group aloud, then the other. Ask, "Which number is less?" Circle that group: it has fewer. Tell the children that fewer means not as many.

K-606.say: "Each box has two numbers. Which number is greater, which one means more? Color the greater number."
K-606.first: Write the numbers 1 to 20 on the board. Do the first box together: find both numbers on the board and ask, "Which one comes later when we count?" That one is greater. Color it.
K-606.stuck: Have the child count aloud from one and stop at the first of the two numbers that comes up; the other number is the greater one.

K:before-after-back.say: "Each number has a neighbor before it and a neighbor after it. Write the number that comes just before and the number that comes just after."
K:before-after-back.first: Write the numbers 1 to 20 in a row on the board and leave them there. Do the first one together: find the number on the board, point to the number before it and the number after it, and write them on the page.
K:before-after-back.stuck: Walk to the board with the child and have the child put a finger on the number: one step to the left is the number before, one step to the right is the number after.

K-022.say: "Each row has two numbers with an empty box between them. Write the number that comes in the middle."
K-022.first: Write the numbers 1 to 20 in a row on the board. Do the first row together: find both numbers on the board and point to the one between them. Write it in the empty box.
K-022.stuck: Have the child count up from the first number: "Fourteen… fifteen." The number they say next is the one in the middle.

K-023.say: "This is a countdown, like for a rocket: 10, 9, 8 and down to 1. Some numbers are missing. Write each missing number."
K-023.first: Count down from 10 to 1 together, with a quiet "blast off" at the end. Do the first strip together, pointing to each box, and say the number at each empty box.
K-023.stuck: Have the child say the countdown from 10 while touching each box; the number they say at an empty box is the one to write.

K:shape-naming.say: "Look at the code at the top. It tells you which color each shape gets. Color every shape in the picture in the color the code shows."
K:shape-naming.first: Make sure every child has the crayons the code shows. Go through the code together: point to each shape, have the class name it, and say its color. Find one shape in the picture and color it together. Tell the children to do one kind of shape at a time.
K:shape-naming.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the shape and look for the same shape in the code. A shape that is bigger, smaller, or turned is still the same shape.

K-368.say: "Look at each shape. It may be turned or skinny, but it is still the same shape. Circle its name."
K-368.first: Draw a circle, a triangle, a square, and a rectangle on the board and name them. Do the first shape together: count its sides and read the three names next to it. Circle the right one.
K-368.stuck: Have the child count the sides with a finger: 3 sides is a triangle; 4 sides of the same length is a square; 4 sides, two long and two short, is a rectangle; round with no sides is a circle.

K:days-of-week.say: "There are seven days in a week. On this page the days are mixed up. The first day already has a 1. Number the other days from 2 to 7, in the order they come."
K:days-of-week.first: Say the days of the week together, starting with the day that is marked 1 on the page. Read all the day names on the page aloud and have the children point to each. Find the day that comes second together and write a 2 next to it.
K:days-of-week.stuck: Say the days in order with the child, beginning with the day marked 1, and stop after each one so the child can find its word. Read the words for a child who cannot read them yet; the first letters help.

K-337.say: "The days of the week go down the ladder in order. Some days are already written. Find the missing days in the word box at the top and copy them onto the empty lines."
K-337.first: Say the days of the week together, starting with Sunday. Read the days already on the ladder aloud. Do the first empty line together: "Sunday, then…?" Find Monday in the word box and copy it letter by letter.
K-337.stuck: Say the days in order with the child, pointing down the ladder, and stop at the empty line. Help the child find the word in the box by its first letter.

K:word-picture-match.say: "Read each word. Then draw a line from the word to its picture."
K:word-picture-match.first: Name all the pictures together. Do the first word on the board: point to each letter, say its sound, and blend the sounds into the word. Ask, "Which picture is that?" Draw the line together.
K:word-picture-match.stuck: Have the child say the sound of each letter and then say the sounds faster. If that does not work, ask for the first sound only and look for the pictures that begin with it. Read the word for the child if they are still stuck.

picture-vocabulary-k225-2.first: Read the words on the page aloud and have the class read each one after you. Name the pictures together: bus, can (a soup can), key, fig, fox, bun (the bread). Do the first word together and draw the line.

picture-vocabulary-k225-3.first: Read the words on the page aloud and have the class read each one after you. Name the pictures together: bag, dog, fan, bun (the bread), egg, key. Do the first word together and draw the line.

picture-vocabulary-k225-4.first: Read the words on the page aloud and have the class read each one after you. Name the pictures together: cap, fan, bee, hen, hot (the hot sun), jam. Do the first word together and draw the line.

K:cvc-build.say: "Next to each picture are the letters of its word, but they are mixed up. Say the word, listen to its sounds, and write the letters in the right order."
K:cvc-build.first: Name all the pictures together. Do the first word on the board: say the word slowly and ask, "What is the first sound? The next sound? The last sound?" Write a letter for each sound and read the word together.
K:cvc-build.stuck: Have the child say the word slowly and hold up one finger for each sound. Ask which of the letters makes the first sound, and cross each letter out when it is used. Then have the child read the word they wrote.

K-224.say: "Each word on this page has a gap in the middle: one letter is missing. Say the picture's name, listen for the sound in the middle, and write its letter."
K-224.first: Name all the pictures together. On the page for everyone they are fig, dog, pig, leg, fox, hat, cat, and bus. Do the first word on the board: say the word slowly, point to each letter as you say its sound, and stop at the empty space. Ask, "Which sound belongs here? Which letter makes it?" Write it in and read the word together.
K-224.stuck: Say the word slowly and stretch the sound in the middle: "p-iii-g." The missing letter is always one of the vowels: a, e, i, o, or u. Write the five vowels on the board for the child to choose from.

K-231.first: Name all the pictures together. On the page for everyone they are frog, fox, bus, sun, star, and ball. Do the first word on the board: say the word slowly and ask, "What is the first sound? The next sound? The last sound?" Write a letter for each sound and read the word together.

word-building-k224-2.first: Name all the pictures together: fig, bun (the bread), jet, jam, lid, dog, cap, fox. Do the first word on the board: say the word slowly, point to each letter as you say its sound, and stop at the empty space. Ask, "Which sound belongs here? Which letter makes it?" Write it in and read the word together.

word-building-k224-4.first: Name all the pictures together: dog, bag, bed, leg, jug, bus, bat, fig. Do the first word on the board: say the word slowly, point to each letter as you say its sound, and stop at the empty space. Ask, "Which sound belongs here? Which letter makes it?" Write it in and read the word together.

word-building-k224-5.first: Name all the pictures together: lid, bed, dog, bus, fan, fox, fig, bun (the bread). Do the first word on the board: say the word slowly, point to each letter as you say its sound, and stop at the empty space. Ask, "Which sound belongs here? Which letter makes it?" Write it in and read the word together.

word-building-k231-2.first: Name all the pictures together: fig, lid, bee, bus, cup, jam. Do the first word on the board: say the word slowly and ask, "What is the first sound? The next sound? The last sound?" Write a letter for each sound and read the word together. "Bee" has two e's that make one sound.

word-building-k231-3.first: Name all the pictures together: ham, jar, egg, hot (the hot sun), ant, jet. Do the first word on the board: say the word slowly and ask, "What is the first sound? The next sound? The last sound?" Write a letter for each sound and read the word together. "Egg" ends with two g's.

word-building-k231-4.first: Name all the pictures together: can, jet, cup, bun (the bread), lid, cat. Do the first word on the board: say the word slowly and ask, "What is the first sound? The next sound? The last sound?" Write a letter for each sound and read the word together.

K:combine-groups.say: "In each box there are two groups. Count all the things in both groups together, and write how many there are in all."
K:combine-groups.first: Do the first box together: count the first group aloud and keep counting through the second group without starting over. Ask, "How many in all?" Write the number on the board.
K:combine-groups.stuck: Have the child touch each picture while counting and keep going from the first group into the second. If the child starts again at one for the second group, count with them once.

K:number-bonds-k.say: "A number bond shows a number and the two parts that make it. The whole is on top, and the two parts are below. One number is missing. Find it and write it in the dashed circle."
K:number-bonds-k.first: Draw the first number bond on the board. Point to the top circle and say, "This is the whole." Point to the two circles below: "These are the two parts." Show it with fingers: "The whole is 5. One part is 2. How many are in the other part?" Write the answer in the dashed circle.
K:number-bonds-k.stuck: Have the child draw dots: as many as the whole. Cross out as many as the part that is shown and count what is left. If the whole is the number that is missing, count both parts together.

K-276.say: "A number bond shows a number and the two parts that make it. On this page the two parts are there, and the whole is missing. Put the two parts together and write the whole in the dashed circle."
K-276.first: Draw the first number bond on the board. Point to the two parts and ask, "How many is that together?" Count both parts with fingers and write the whole in the dashed circle.
K-276.stuck: Have the child draw dots for each part under the number bond and count all the dots. That number is the whole.

K:classify-count-kinds.say: "This is an I Spy picture. Many different things are mixed together. Count each kind and write its number."
K:classify-count-kinds.first: Look at the first kind together: point to its little picture next to the answer box. Find every one of that kind in the big picture and cross each one out as the class counts aloud. Write the number in the box.
K:classify-count-kinds.stuck: Have the child do one kind at a time and put a small mark on each one as it is counted. If the count is off, count the marks together.

K:seasons.say: "A tree looks different in winter, spring, summer, and fall. Each box has a bare tree. Draw what belongs on the tree in that season."
K:seasons.first: Make sure every child has crayons. Read the name of each season aloud and point to its box. Talk about each one for a moment: "What does a tree look like in winter? What grows on it in spring? What does it have in summer? What happens to the leaves in fall?" Then the children draw on the bare trees, one box at a time, and color them.
K:seasons.stuck: Ask the child one question about the season: "Is it warm or cold? Are there leaves on the tree?" Any drawing that fits the season is right; where you live, winter may not mean snow.

K-207.say: "At the top are clothes. At the bottom are two boxes: Summer and Winter. Draw a line from each piece of clothing to the season we wear it in."
K-207.first: Read the two boxes aloud and name every piece of clothing together. Do the first one together: ask, "Do we wear this when it is hot or when it is cold?" Draw the line to its box.
K-207.stuck: Ask the child, "Would you wear this to the beach or in the snow?" Where you live, winter may not mean snow; let the child explain.

K-338.say: "Each card has three pictures that belong to one season. Under them are four signs: a snowflake for winter, a flower for spring, a sun for summer, and a leaf for fall. Circle the sign of the season."
K-338.first: Point to the four signs and name the seasons together. Do the first card together: name the three pictures and ask, "When do we see these?" Circle the sign.
K-338.stuck: Ask the child about one picture at a time: "Is it hot or cold then? Are there flowers or falling leaves?"

K:story-sequencing.stuck: Ask the child to find the picture where the story starts, where nothing has happened yet. Then ask, "What happens after that?" Have the child tell the story aloud; if it makes sense, the order is right.

K:tally-marks.say: "Tally marks are a quick way to count. Make one mark for each picture. The fifth mark goes across the other four, like a gate."
K:tally-marks.first: Draw tally marks on the board while the class counts to five: four marks standing up, and the fifth one across them. Do the first box together: count the pictures and draw one mark for each.
K:tally-marks.stuck: Have the child cross out one picture and draw one mark, then the next picture and the next mark. Count the marks together at the end. If the child draws five standing marks before the one across, show the group of five on the board again.

K-015.say: "Each box has tally marks. Count them and write the number."
K-015.first: Draw tally marks on the board while the class counts to five: four marks standing up and the fifth one across them. Do the first box together: count the marks and write the number. A bundle of five with a line across counts as five.
K-015.stuck: Have the child touch each mark and count. For a bundle with a line across, say "five" and count on from there: six, seven…

K-025.say: "On the left are numbers. On the right are tally marks. Draw a line from each number to its tally marks."
K-025.first: Draw a bundle of five tally marks on the board. Count the first group of marks together and find its number on the left. Draw the line.
K-025.stuck: Have the child touch each mark and count. For a bundle with a line across, say "five" and count on from there: six, seven…

K:fact-fluency-colour-code.say: "Every shape on this page has a little math problem in it. Find the answer, look for that number in the code, and color the shape in that color."
K:fact-fluency-colour-code.first: Make sure every child has the crayons the code names. Do one shape together: read the problem, find the answer with fingers, and write the answer small next to the problem. Find that number in the code and color the shape. Tell the children to check the sign first: plus or minus.
K:fact-fluency-colour-code.stuck: Let the child use fingers or draw dots to find the answer. Have the child write the answer in the shape before looking at the code. If the answer is not in the code, the child should work the problem again.

K:category-odd-one-out.say: "In each row, the shapes are all the same but one. Find the one that does not belong and circle it."
K:category-odd-one-out.first: Do the first row together. Point to the shapes one by one and name them: "star, star, star…" Ask, "Which one is not a star?" Circle it and have a child say why it does not belong.
K:category-odd-one-out.stuck: Have the child point to the first shape and then to each of the others, asking, "Is this the same shape?" If the child chooses another one and can give a good reason, accept it.

1:one-ten-more-less.say: "Look at the number in the middle. On the left, write the number that is 10 less. On the right, write the number that is 10 more."
1:one-ten-more-less.first: Do the first one on the board. Ask: "Ten more than 36. Which digit changes, the tens or the ones?" Show that only the tens digit changes: 26, 36, 46. Count by tens from another number together, for example 7, 17, 27, 37.
1:one-ten-more-less.stuck: If the classroom has a hundreds chart, have the child find the number on it: the number straight above is 10 less, and the number straight below is 10 more. Without a chart, have the child cover the ones digit and change the tens digit by one.

G1-131.say: "Look at the number in the middle. On the left, write the number that is 1 less. On the right, write the number that is 1 more."
G1-131.first: Write 1 to 100 in rows of ten on the board, or point to the class hundred chart. Do the first one together: find the number, step one back for 1 less and one on for 1 more.
G1-131.stuck: Have the child count aloud up to the number and say the next one: that is 1 more. The one said just before it is 1 less.

G1-132@w.first: Do the first one on the board: read the number in the middle and ask, "Ten more: which digit changes, the tens or the ones?" Show that only the tens digit changes, one more ten for ten more and one less ten for ten less. Count by tens from another number together, for example 7, 17, 27, 37.

2:word-classes.say: "A noun names a person, an animal, a place, or a thing. A verb is something you can do. An adjective tells what something is like. Read the nine words and write each one in the right bin."
2:word-classes.first: Read the nine words aloud together. Sort one of each kind on the board with a test sentence: "I can see a ___" for a noun, "I can ___" for a verb, and "The dolphin is ___" for an adjective. The nouns on this page have a little picture next to them. Cross out each word once it is in a bin.
2:word-classes.stuck: Read the word to the child and have the child try the three test sentences aloud. The one that sounds right tells the bin. For your own reference, on the page for everyone the nouns are dolphin, seagull, and giraffe; the verbs are swim, sit, and run; the adjectives are slow, purple, and red.

G2-275@w.first: Read all the words on the page aloud with the class. Do the first two words together: "Is it a naming word, an action word, or a describing word?" Write each in its bin.
G2-275@w.say: "A noun names a person, an animal, a place, or a thing. A verb is something you can do. An adjective tells what something is like. Read every word and write each one in the right bin."
G2-275@w.stuck: Read the word to the child and try three test sentences aloud: "I see a ___." (a noun), "I can ___." (a verb), "It is ___." (an adjective). The one that sounds right tells the bin.

G2-286@w.first: Read all twelve words aloud with the class. Do the first two words together: "Is it a noun, a verb, or an adjective?" Write each in its bin.
